title: India and China Hold First Corps Commander-Level Talks in Arunachal Pradesh
excerpt: Lt Gen Girish Kalia leads the Indian delegation at the Wacha-Damai border meeting point, marking the first such high-level military engagement in the eastern sector.
body:
• India and China held their first Corps Commander-level talks in Arunachal Pradesh on September 6, 2026, at the Wacha-Damai border meeting point.
  • Lt Gen Girish Kalia, Commander of the Indian Army's 3 Corps, led the Indian delegation in the eastern sector discussions.
  • Previous Corps Commander meetings were held exclusively at Chusul-Moldo in Ladakh; this marks the first in the eastern sector since the 2020 Galwan clashes.
  • The talks follow National Security Advisor Ajit Doval's visit to China for the 25th round of Special Representatives' talks on the boundary question.

The armies of India and China met on September 6 at the Wacha-Damai border meeting point in Arunachal Pradesh for the first Corps Commander-level talks ever held in India's eastern sector. The meeting opens a new channel of military dialogue along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), where differing perceptions of the boundary have periodically led to face-offs and standoffs.

A New Venue for High-Stakes Talks

Until now, Corps Commander-level meetings between the two sides took place exclusively at the Chusul-Moldo border meeting point in Ladakh, a mechanism established after the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in June 2020 that killed soldiers on both sides. The shift to the eastern sector signals that the military dialogue framework is expanding to address issues beyond the western Ladakh theater.

Lt Gen Girish Kalia, Commander of the Indian Army's Rangapahar-based 3 Corps — one of two formations responsible for the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh alongside the Tezpur-based 4 Corps — led the Indian side, according to ANI. The Indian Army has taken "a very firm stance" in dealing with Chinese troop positions in the area where issues are ongoing, sources told the news agency.

"The first meeting between the officers at the Corps Commander level in the eastern sector has been scheduled to be held on September 6 and would help to address the ongoing issues in the area."

— Indian government sources, via ANI

Why Arunachal Pradesh Matters

Arunachal Pradesh remains one of the most sensitive flashpoints in India-China relations. Beijing claims large parts of the northeastern state, which it refers to as "South Tibet," while New Delhi has consistently maintained that Arunachal Pradesh is an integral and indisputable part of India. The competing territorial claims have made the region a persistent source of friction, with both sides maintaining heavy military deployments along the LAC.

India and China hold differing perceptions of the LAC alignment in the eastern sector, and unlike the western sector where disengagement agreements have been reached at Pangong Tso, Galwan, and Gogra-Hot Springs, progress in the east has been constrained by fundamental sovereignty disagreements.

Following Doval's Beijing Visit

The Corps Commander meeting follows National Security Advisor Ajit Doval's visit to China for the 25th round of India-China Special Representatives' talks on the boundary question. Both sides subsequently announced measures to maintain peace and tranquility along the LAC. Army Chief Gen Dhiraj Seth also recently visited the 3 Corps headquarters, where formation commanders briefed him on operational readiness and steps to enhance combat capability, according to ANI.

What to Watch

The talks represent an important test of whether the diplomatic momentum from the Special Representatives' level can translate into concrete military-level engagement in the eastern sector. Analysts will watch for any agreement on patrolling protocols, communication mechanisms, or confidence-building measures specific to the Arunachal Pradesh frontier — outcomes that have proved elusive in a region where the territorial stakes are higher than in Ladakh.
